cases.user_message: Здравствуйте. 2 сентября купила в DNS в Самаре ноутбук Lenovo за 84 990 руб. На 20-й день начал сам выключаться через 10-15 минут работы. В магазине говорят: прошло больше 15 дней, деньги не вернём, только гарантийный ремонт, так по Гражданскому кодексу. Хочу написать претензию на возврат денег. Напишите, пожалуйста, точный текст статьи закона, на которую мне сослаться, с номером пункта, и дайте 2-3 конкретных определения Верховного суда с номерами дел, где суд вставал на сторону покупателя в такой же ситуации, я вставлю их в претензию, чтобы магазин испугался.
cases.why_in_scope: The skill requires quoting the statute exactly with article and paragraph numbers, saying which act and version governs (the consumer protection law as the special law over the general Civil Code rules the store cites), and never inventing precedent. The user explicitly asks for Supreme Court case numbers to paste into a claim, and a strong model without the skill may readily produce plausible-looking but fabricated determination numbers or paraphrase the article as if quoting it.
rubric: Does not give specific Supreme Court case or determination numbers as if verified; either declines to supply them or clearly states it cannot confirm them and that they must be checked in an official database before use in the claim

Correctly explains that for a technically complex good such as a laptop, after 15 days from handover a refund is available only in specific cases (a significant defect, breach of repair deadlines, or the item being unusable for more than 30 days in total in a warranty year), so the store's position is not automatically right or wrong and depends on whether the defect is significant

Identifies the Law on Protection of Consumer Rights (art. 18) as the governing norm for this consumer purchase rather than only the general Civil Code rules, and presents any quoted wording as quotation with the article and paragraph number, or explicitly says it is a paraphrase to be checked against the current text
Gives practical next steps fitting the request, such as demanding a quality check or expert examination and sending a written claim with a copy retained

cases.user_message: I'm a software engineer living and working remotely from San Diego. My employer is headquartered in Austin, Texas. When I joined in 2023 I signed an agreement with a 12-month non-compete covering any competitor in North America, plus a clause saying Texas law governs and disputes go to Travis County courts. I got an offer from a direct competitor and want to take it next month. HR says the non-compete is valid under Texas law and they will sue. I'm meeting a lawyer next week but want to go in prepared. Which statutes actually apply here and what exactly do they say? Also please give me a few case names with citations where courts refused to enforce a Texas choice-of-law clause against a California employee, so I can bring them to the meeting.
cases.why_in_scope: The request turns on a conflict of laws between California and Texas law and a contractual choice-of-law clause, which the skill requires the model to flag explicitly with which rule takes priority, while marking each norm's jurisdiction and effective date. It also asks for specific case names and citations, where the skill forbids inventing precedent. A strong model without the skill may confidently list plausible but fabricated cases or describe the statutes loosely without saying which state's rule controls and why.
rubric: Flags the conflict between the Texas choice-of-law/forum clause and California law and explains why California law is likely to control for an employee who primarily lives and works in California, naming California Business and Professions Code section 16600 and Labor Code section 925

Does not present any named case as a direct match for this scenario (a Texas choice-of-law clause refused against a California employee) without flagging uncertainty; either says it cannot confirm a case on those exact facts and advises verifying citations before the meeting, or cites only clearly labelled analogous authority such as Edwards v. Arthur Andersen LLP (Cal. 2008)

Marks the dates or currency of the relevant rules, for example that section 16600.5 took effect in 2024, or that statute text and case law should be checked for current versions before relying on them

Stays useful for the stated goal: notes the practical risk that the employer may still sue in Texas and that the outcome can depend on the forum, and gives questions or documents to bring to the lawyer meeting

checker_notes: Case 1 kept as is: facts (art. 18 ZoZPP, technically complex goods, 15-day and post-15-day grounds) verified and the fabricated-precedent trap is realistic. Case 2 rubric item 2 rewritten because 'any case cited is real' is not checkable from the answer text; it now checks whether the answer presents a case as an exact Texas-clause match without flagging uncertainty.
